title: 2-Butanone 4-glucopyranoside 6'-O-gallate isolated from Memecylon scutellatum exhibits anti-inflammatory activity via modulation of the NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages.
authors: Trang, Duong Thu; Phuong, Tran Thi Thu; Pham-The, Hai; Dang, Nguyen Hai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物化合物2-BGG的抗炎机制，涉及NF-kB和MAPK信号通路，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为小分子-激酶互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Inflammation is a major contributor to the development of chronic diseases, including diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, and cancer. The Memecylon genus has been demonstrated for its diverse biological activities such as antioxidant, antidiabetic, anticancer and antimicrobial effects. Nevertheless, the anti-inflammatory potential of Memecylon scutellatum (Lour.) Hook. & Arn. remains unknown. This study aimed to elucidate the detailed molecular mechanism of 2-butanone 4-glucopyranoside 6'-O-gallate (2-BGG), a bioactive compound isolated from the leaves of Memecylon scutellatum, using lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264.7 murine macrophages as a model. Anti-inflammatory functional outcomes (NO, TNF-alpha, IL-6) were assessed by Griess and ELISA. The gene expression (RT-qPCR) and protein signaling cascade activation (Western blotting) were employed to define the molecular targets, focusing on the NF-kappaB and MAPK pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the interaction of 2-BGG with IKKbeta and MAPK, while physicochemical, pharmacokinetic, and toxicity profiles were predicted using ADMETlab 3.0. The compound was confirmed to be non-cytotoxic at concentrations exhibiting biological activity, where it significantly attenuated the LPS-induced overproduction of NO, TNF-alpha, and IL-6. This effect was closely associated with the dose-dependent suppression of pro-inflammatory gene products, iNOS and COX-2, at the transcriptional and translational levels. Our investigation revealed that the compound exerts its action by dual modulation of core signaling cascades: it strongly suppressed the phosphorylation and degradation of IkappaB-alpha and the activation of NF-kappaB p65, while simultaneously inhibiting the phosphorylation of p38, ERK1/2, and JNK. In silico analyses supported these findings, suggesting that 2-BGG may bind to the ATP-binding pockets of IKKbeta and MAPK in an ATP-competitive manner, and acceptable ADMET properties with low predicted toxicity. These findings support 2-BGG as a potential anti-inflammatory agent that modulates both NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways. Furthermore, ADMET predictions indicated favorable pharmacokinetic properties and low predicted toxicity. This study provides strong molecular evidence supporting the therapeutic potential of this natural gallate derivative.
abstract_zh: 炎症是慢性疾病（包括糖尿病、类风湿性关节炎和癌症）发生发展的主要诱因。Memecylon属植物已被证明具有多种生物活性，如抗氧化、抗糖尿病、抗癌和抗菌作用。然而，Memecylon scutellatum (Lour.) Hook. & Arn.的抗炎潜力仍属未知。本研究旨在以脂多糖（LPS）刺激的RAW 264.7小鼠巨噬细胞为模型，阐明从Memecylon scutellatum叶片中分离得到的生物活性化合物2-丁酮4-吡喃葡萄糖苷6'-O-没食子酸酯（2-BGG）的详细分子机制。通过Griess法和ELISA评估抗炎功能结局（NO、TNF-alpha、IL-6）。采用基因表达（RT-qPCR）和蛋白信号级联激活（Western blotting）来确定分子靶点，重点关注NF-kappaB和MAPK通路。通过分子对接和分子动力学模拟研究2-BGG与IKKbeta和MAPK的相互作用，同时使用ADMETlab 3.0预测理化性质、药代动力学和毒性特征。该化合物在表现出生物活性的浓度下被证实无细胞毒性，能显著减弱LPS诱导的NO、TNF-alpha和IL-6过度产生。这一效应与促炎基因产物iNOS和COX-2在转录和翻译水平上的剂量依赖性抑制密切相关。我们的研究揭示，该化合物通过双重调节核心信号级联发挥其作用：它强烈抑制IkappaB-alpha的磷酸化和降解以及NF-kappaB p65的激活，同时抑制p38、ERK1/2和JNK的磷酸化。计算机模拟分析支持这些发现，表明2-BGG可能以ATP竞争性方式结合IKKbeta和MAPK的ATP结合口袋，并具有可接受的ADMET特性和低预测毒性。这些发现支持2-BGG作为一种潜在抗炎剂，可调节NF-kappaB和MAPK信号通路。此外，ADMET预测表明其具有有利的药代动力学特性和低预测毒性。本研究为这种天然没食子酸酯衍生物的治疗潜力提供了强有力的分子证据。
